items.title: Miners tumble as ASX slumps ahead of jobs data; Anthropic prices IPO above range
paras: Advertisement Updated Business Markets World markets Miners tumble as ASX slumps ahead of jobs data; Anthropic prices IPO above range Staff writers Updated November 19, 2026 — 10:52am , first published 5:17am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A The Australian sharemarket has opened sharply lower after a fifth-straight drop for the S&P 500 dragged Wall Street to its longest losing streak since June, with AI stocks continuing to weigh on global indexes.

The S&P/ASX 200 was down 105.2 points, or 1.2 per cent, in early trade, with mining stocks tumbling as the price of copper, seen as integral to the AI boom, fell more than 5 per cent. Unemployment figures for October will be released at 11.30am AEDT. The ASX fell by 0.7 per cent on Wednesday, its fifth-straight losing session.

Wall Street is on an unsteady footing as doubts over AI companies hover. AP Anthropic released pricing for its Wall Street debut after the closing bell in New York. Bloomberg reported the stock will be set at $US83 per share, above its target range of $US70 to $US78 per share, valuing the company at around $US1.5 trillion ($2.2 trillion). The company is set to start trading on Friday morning (AEDT).

Mining stocks plunged in early trade on the ASX with BHP down 4.3 per cent, Rio Tinto down 3.2 per cent and Fortescue down 1.1 per cent. Copper fell 5.7 per cent on the London Metals Exchange to the lowest since April. Tin — another key input in the artificial intelligence industry — shed 5 per cent in London. The moves came after Stan Druckenmiller, one of the most high-profile cheerleaders for copper’s AI trade, said he’d turned bearish on the metal, adding to a chorus of concerns about AI’s growth trajectory. The rout adds to a week of extreme volatility in metals markets. Gold miners also lost ground, with Northern Star down 3.9 per cent and Evolution Mining down 3.8 per cent.
Financial stocks are steady in early trade with Commonwealth Bank up 0.1 per cent, Westpac flat, ANZ Bank down 0.1 per cent and National Australia Bank down 0.3 per cent.

Energy stocks are lower. Oil prices slumped overnight as weaker risk appetite, rising US inventories and ample supplies outweighed Middle East tensions. Woodside Energy was down 2.4 per cent, Santos slipped 3.2 per cent in early trade, Ampol fell 1.6 per cent and Viva Energy was down 2 per cent.
Investor pressure sent technology stocks lower with WiseTech down 0.8 per cent, Xero dropping 0.9 per cent, Technology One losing 1.8 per cent and Codan sliding 2.7 per cent.

Overnight, the S&P 500 fell 0.2 per cent after zigzagging between gains and losses through the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 561 points, or 1.1 per cent, while the Nasdaq composite added 0.4 per cent.

Nvidia was once again at the centre of Wall Street’s moves. Its stock initially jumped 2.7 per cent after the chip company reported stronger profit and revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected but that gain was wiped out and it closed 2.9 per cent lower. Perhaps more importantly, it also gave a forecast for revenue in the current quarter that was better than expected.

The question is whether Nvidia’s big growth can continue despite the turmoil created by the sudden downfall of Jensen Huang, its former CEO and co-founder. He had an immense personality that drew attention and investment to AI, and he built Nvidia into a company so big that it helped to fund some of the industry’s growth itself.

“Our momentum is real,” Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, told investors and financial analysts after announcing the company’s latest results. “Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed. We’ve got this.”
The encouraging numbers and words coming from Nvidia failed to create lasting gains for the price of its stock or for others across the industry.

Micron Technology, whose sales of memory chips exploded with the AI boom, went from an early rise of 1.5 per cent to a drop of 1 per cent. CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and rents access to them out to customers over the cloud, sank 4.1 per cent and has lost nearly a third of its value so far this year.

The entire industry has been swinging recently. Besides criticism that AI stock prices simply shot too high in their frenzy, the industry is facing worries that this month’s sweeping victories for Democrats in the US midterm elections could mean more regulation for it.

Stocks of oil companies weighed on Wall Street due to drops in oil prices. But oil’s fall also helped pull yields down in the bond market, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 5.06 per cent from 5.10 per cent late on Tuesday.

High yields have made mortgages more expensive to get, which has chilled the housing industry. But they’ve moderated over the last month, and a report said homebuilders broke ground on more projects last month than economists expected.
In stock markets abroad, indexes fell in Europe following a mixed finish in Asia.

Expectations are high that the Federal Reserve in Washington will raise its own interest rate when it meets next month, after it made no move last month. Notes released Wednesday from the Fed’s latest meeting indicated some officials are considering a larger increase to rates than usual in December.

items.title: Canada’s major immigration policy U-turn is a warning to Australia
paras: In the years since the pandemic, Canada’s migration system has become one of the most talked about in the world, as net overseas migration first surged to all-time highs, then dropped back to well below pre-pandemic levels.

Between the final pre-pandemic reading in the December quarter of 2019 and the peak in the March quarter of 2024, Canada’s rate of net overseas migration rose by over 704,000, one of the most meteoric rises in migration in per capita terms in the history of the world.
Since then, the magnitude of the drop has been equally large in magnitude, with the size of the net intake falling by 87.3% to 151,800.

items.title: Syngenis joins WA research heavyweights in RNA medicine push

Share A A A For most pharmaceutical companies, developing a medicine for a single patient would seem like commercial madness. However, Perth biotechnology player Syngenis Labs is helping turn that conventional wisdom on its head. It has joined forces with two Western Australian medical research giants to advance treatments for children with rare genetic diseases, sometimes so rare that only one patient may need the medicine.

The company has teamed up with the WA-based Perron Institute and the Personalised Medicine Centre (PMC), a joint initiative between Perron and Murdoch University, to establish a specialised preclinical safety-testing platform for experimental RNA medicines targeting rare genetic and neurological diseases affecting the brain and spinal cord.

Murdoch University’s Associate Professor May Aung-Htut will oversee next-generation RNA medicine safety testing at the Personalised Medicine Centre, backed by Syngenis Labs and the Perron Institute. The new initiative aims to tackle one of drug development’s biggest hurdles – establishing whether promising laboratory discoveries are sufficiently safe to progress towards human trials – potentially opening another commercial avenue for Syngenis ahead of its proposed ASX listing.

Founded in Perth in 2020 by RNA researcher Professor Rakesh Veedu, Syngenis manufactures specialised genetic materials at its Bentley Technology Park laboratories, supplying universities, researchers, biotechnology companies and diagnostic developers.

Steering the commercial charge is managing director Thomas Hanly, who’s looking to turn Syngenis’s specialist RNA and DNA expertise into a scalable biotechnology business spanning drug discovery, manufacturing and personalised medicine.

The company’s products include custom-designed strands of DNA and RNA, known as oligonucleotides, used to investigate diseases, create genetic tests and develop experimental medicines. Some detect genetic variations, while others can interfere with biological instructions responsible for disease, potentially silencing harmful messages rather than simply treating symptoms. That makes them particularly promising for rare inherited disorders affecting only a handful of patients worldwide.

Syngenis operates three divisions: Syngenis Manufacturing - its revenue-generating DNA and RNA production business - Syngenis AI, which identifies and designs potential genetic medicines and Syngenis Ventures, which invests in biotechnology companies capable of commercialising its expertise.

Syngenis Labs managing director Thomas Hanly said: “ With tens of thousands of Australian children living with rare diseases and many families still searching for a diagnosis, the opportunity to develop highly targeted, potentially life-changing medicines is substantial. Working alongside the Perron Institute and the Personalised Medicine Centre, we want to remove the technical, financial and infrastructure barriers that prevent promising discoveries from reaching patients.”

Based at the PMC on Murdoch University’s South Street campus, the safety-testing platform will combine laboratory testing and studies in living systems to investigate experimental RNA medicines, identify potential safety problems earlier and determine which candidates warrant further investment.
PMC research fellows Dr Jessica Cale and Dr Kelly Martinovich will lead the work under the guidance of PMC Molecular Therapy Lab co-lead associate professor Dr May Aung-Htut.
By bringing safety testing closer to drug discovery, the partners hope to cut costs, reduce delays and accelerate promising treatments through early development.

Hanly believes the collaboration could help remove technical and financial barriers preventing genetic treatments from reaching patients, with the longer-term goal of making personalised medicines commercially and clinically viable for a much broader population.

Underscoring the growing promise of next-generation RNA medicines, serious financial firepower in the form of the Perron Institute is now flowing into WA’s rapidly expanding rare-disease research sector.

Established in 1982, the neuroscience heavyweight is Western Australia’s longest-established medical research institute and a significant Australian nucleic-acid research centre, with programs spanning motor neurone disease, Parkinson’s disease, other rare diseases and youth mental health.

Scientists at Perron helped pioneer gene-targeting technology using antisense oligonucleotides – specially designed molecules that intercept faulty RNA instructions – paving the way for the first US FDA-approved treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Two further treatments subsequently gained approval based on the underlying research.

Notably, Perron is also a strategic shareholder in Syngenis, while Syngenis’s founder and chief technology officer, Professor Veedu, has longstanding research ties with the institute and a deep background in personalised medicine.

Adding even more financial muscle to WA’s burgeoning rare-disease sector, the unrelated Stan Perron Charitable Foundation has committed $221 million over the next decade to establish the Rare Care Comprehensive Centre at Perth Children’s Hospital, with the PMC expected to play an important role in its Treatments and Trials Flagship program.

Separately, the PMC has also secured a $3.99 million Medical Research Future Fund grant to expand as a national facility developing antisense oligonucleotide medicines, including treatments tailored to rare genetic conditions.
While neither commitment represents funding awarded directly to Syngenis, the sheer scale of investment underlines the scientific and financial muscle gathering around personalised medicine.

Perhaps sensing a shift in the sands, a prospective customer is already waiting in the wings. Privately held Black Swan Biotech, another WA company developing RNA-based treatments for motor neurone disease, is expected to become a major user of the facility.

Personalised Medicine Centre director Professor Anthony Akkari believes the shared testing capability could shorten the journey towards clinical trials, while Perron chief executive Steve Arnott sees it as a resource for multiple research teams.
For Syngenis, however, the attraction is not just the science. The collaboration also plays neatly into its manufacturing plans.

Its existing business supplies research-grade and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-grade genetic materials, including specialist chemistries for experimental RNA treatments. GLP sets quality standards for laboratory studies, particularly drug safety testing, while Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) governs controlled production of medicines and ingredients for clinical use.

Syngenis is now taking that strategy up another notch, building what it says will be Australia’s first GMP facility dedicated to clinical-grade oligonucleotide manufacturing, with regulatory approval targeted for 2027, subject to Therapeutic Goods Administration inspection and applicable licensing requirements.
Once approved, the facility could give Syngenis a foothold across the development chain, from early research and safety testing to manufacturing clinical-grade molecules for human trials.

Under its collaboration with Perron and Murdoch, Syngenis will contribute funding and manufacture GLP-grade genetic sequences for the PMC’s testing platform, with plans to supply GMP-grade material once operational.
The partners also aim to reduce Australia’s dependence on overseas drug-development facilities, building a more complete domestic pathway from laboratory discovery to clinical trials.

For Syngenis, the commercial upside could be significant, potentially opening a new revenue stream through preclinical safety-testing services while driving demand for its specialist RNA and DNA manufacturing capabilities.
And the company has another iron in the personalised medicine fire, having snapped up a one-third stake in Gene-S Dx through its investment arm, Syngenis Ventures, in September.

The business was established alongside the Perron Institute and the founders of Gene S, acquiring the original Gene S operation - now called Gene-S Dx - and its Rosa pharmacogenomics platform, which aims to help tailor medicines to patients based on their genetic profiles.

Unlike its new partnership with PMC, which aims to help develop new genetic treatments, Gene-S Dx uses patients’ genetic information to help doctors select existing medicines and doses better suited to their individual biology. Its Rosa platform includes RosaMind, a genetic test focused on mental health medications.
Syngenis also brings its chemistry and manufacturing expertise to the venture, potentially generating recurring revenue from components for Gene-S Dx’s genetic test kits.
Together, the initiatives give Syngenis a foot in both camps of personalised medicine – improving how existing medicines are prescribed and helping develop treatments that may not yet exist.

And the commercial opportunity stretches well beyond rare genetic disorders. Personalised medicine is already entering mainstream healthcare, with genetic testing helping doctors identify targeted cancer treatments and tailor prescribing decisions. As genetic technologies become cheaper, their applications could spread further into everyday medicine.

The eventual prize could be enormous. According to market forecasts published on Syngenis’ website, the global RNA therapeutics market is projected to surge from US$27 billion in 2025 to US$103 billion by 2035, representing compound annual growth of almost 14 per cent.

Closer to Syngenis’ manufacturing heartland, the global oligonucleotide synthesis market – the specialised genetic materials underpinning RNA medicine development – is forecast to grow from US$3.6 billion to US$10.9 billion by 2033, highlighting the potential demand for the company’s expanding production capabilities.

To bankroll its growth ambitions, Syngenis recently pocketed $4 million through a pre-IPO raise ahead of its proposed ASX listing, targeting growth across precision medicine, RNA therapeutics and oligonucleotide synthesis.

Armed with an established manufacturing business, a clinical-grade facility in development and expanding precision-medicine collaborations, the Perth biotech looks to be assembling the pieces of a business capable of earning its keep at multiple stages of the genetic-medicine value chain.
Its latest collaboration could help clear one of the most stubborn roadblocks between laboratory discovery and human trials, while opening another commercial avenue for the company.
And if the pieces fall into place, Syngenis could find itself helping turn some of medicine’s most challenging genetic discoveries into life-changing treatments – one patient at a time.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

🇮🇳 sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA. The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products,… pic.twitter.com/ZlFiKOfezx

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
paras: Republicans are unanimous Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote Democrats try to prevent quorum, say Thumann lied about not working on media issues.

18 ... ... ... Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) at a hearing on Tuesday, January 28, 2025. Credit: Getty Images | Tom Williams Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) at a hearing on Tuesday, January 28, 2025. Credit: Getty Images | Tom Williams Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote.

All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee’s 13 Democrats were absent. “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” Cruz said at today’s hearing.
Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January.

Although the Senate Commerce Committee generally requires one minority member to be present for nomination votes, a spokesperson for Cruz said Senate rules allow the nomination to be advanced for a vote in the entire chamber. A spokesperson for Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the committee, said in response that “since 2005, Commerce Committee rules required that a quorum include one member of the minority for official action on bill, resolution, or nomination.”

Technically, the committee has operated with no rules during Cruz’s chairmanship because Cruz “failed to pass committee rules” for the current session of Congress, Cantwell’s spokesperson said. “Nevertheless, in practice it has operated in line with rules from the last Congress (and this provision, specifically, since 2005), including that a quorum with a member of the minority party must be present for official action on a nomination or legislation. Until today.”

At a hearing last week, Thumann said she never worked with Carr on media-related topics, leading to accusations that she provided false testimony. “I have not worked with the chairman on any media-related issues,” Thumann said after Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) asked, “Do you support Chairman Carr’s illegal campaign to remove Jimmy Kimmel from the nation’s airwaves?”

“It appears that Ms. Thumann misled the Committee and offered false testimony, seriously calling into question her judgment and character and impeding the Committee’s work in determining whether she should be seated on the Commission,” Luján wrote in a letter to Cruz yesterday. “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related issues,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media-related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount.”

The FCC website describes Thumann as senior counsel to Carr on matters before the Wireline Bureau, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau, and the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau. Emails obtained in a public records request by the group Protect Democracy show she had some involvement in media-related matters.

Thumann provided follow-up responses to senators’ questions this week. She said that her work sometimes includes “reviewing documents or filings in a matter outside of my designated portfolio. However, I did not have any conversations with Paramount, CBS, or Skydance related to the merger.”
Thumann has been referred to as Thumann Severs in the nomination process, but she uses the name Thumann.

Luján wrote that Thumann “played a role in processing informal complaints related to” alleged news distortion on CBS’s 60 Minutes , and that “she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” However, Thumann was only a recipient of the Kimmel-related emails we found in a search of the messages.

The emails do show that Thumann approved language used in a response the FCC gave to complaints about the alleged news distortion in a 60 Minutes interview with Kamala Harris. The response informed people who submitted complaints that they should instead submit comments on an FCC docket that had been set up for the 60 Minutes proceeding.

“Hi Kristi, I have confirmed with the Chairman and Erin that we would like for complainants to be encouraged to resubmit their news distortion complaints in the relevant ECFS [Electronic Comment Filing System] proceeding,” Thumann wrote. “Can you please work on some draft language to send to consumers that would advise them on this step (including how to use ECFS)?”
Democrats announced yesterday that they would try to prevent a quorum for today’s vote. They objected to adding a third Republican to the committee while a Democratic seat remains empty.

“All Democratic members of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee object to the majority stacking independent commissions with Republicans and rushing nominees through the Committee process in this lame duck session with no Democratic pairs,” Cantwell said in a statement.

Cantwell and other Democrats on the committee sent a letter to Cruz urging him to cancel the vote, while quoting his own words from 2014. “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the Democratic committee members said.
Cruz said today that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January. But today is November 18.” Cruz said there is “ample precedent” for advancing nominations in a lame-duck session.

Senate Commerce Committee rules state that a quorum for nomination votes requires a “majority of the members, which includes at least one minority member.” But a Cruz spokesperson pointed to certain clauses regarding committee quorums in Senate rules when contacted by Ars today.

In the Standing Rules of the Senate , paragraph 7 of rule XXVI says that “no measure or matter or recommendation shall be reported from any committee unless a majority of the committee were physically present,” and does not have any requirement for minority members to be present. Elsewhere, the Senate rules say that when a committee reports a measure to the Senate floor, “no point of order shall lie with respect to that measure” as long as the committee took its action “in conformity with the requirements of paragraph 7 of rule XXVI.”

While committees can have different quorum rules, a Cruz spokesperson said this functions as a “cleansing clause” so that “earlier procedural irregularities, such as a violation of a committee rule, cannot be used to invalidate the vote on the Senate floor.”
FCC nominations have traditionally been paired with one Republican and one Democrat when there is an empty seat for each party. But Cruz said that’s not a requirement.

“There’s nothing that requires the president to nominate in pairs… the law merely says that no more than three of the commissioners may be from the same party,” Cruz said during the Republican-only meeting.

The Communications Act prohibits a single party from holding more FCC seats than is necessary to form a majority. It says, “The maximum number of commissioners who may be members of the same political party shall be a number equal to the least number of commissioners which constitutes a majority of the full membership of the Commission.”

Republicans would have a 3-1 majority on the FCC if Thumann is confirmed by the Senate. The sole Democrat, Anna Gomez, would have to leave at the end of 2027 if Trump does not nominate her for another term.

“There is no mandate for the outgoing majority to rush through a partisan FCC nomination in its final weeks… Ms. Thumann Severs’ nomination should be postponed until the next Congress and paired with Commissioner Gomez’s renomination and the nomination of an additional Democratic commissioner,” Democrats told Cruz in their letter this week.

items.title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
paras: No Starshield, no problem Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits Ukraine’s strike used homegrown tech while adapting battlefield lessons from its adversary.

32 ... ... ... Vantor satellite image shows multiple smoke generator vehicles obscuring part of the Crimea Bridge crossing over the Kerch Strait on June 22, 2026. Credit: Vantor Vantor satellite image shows multiple smoke generator vehicles obscuring part of the Crimea Bridge crossing over the Kerch Strait on June 22, 2026. Credit: Vantor Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in.

On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile.

The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities.

During the Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Strait Bridge, the flying mesh network allowed operators located more than 250 kilometers away (155 miles) to remotely guide missiles and drones in evading Russian air defenses while also homing in on the bridge’s weakest structural points, according to the Financial Times .

Ukraine’s takedown of the bridge segment was preceded by weeks of preparatory strikes that systematically destroyed or degraded Russian air defense weapons, radars and electronic warfare equipment arrayed to protect the bridge. The November 15 night attack on the bridge also coincided with the largest Ukrainian overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of the full-scale war, Reuters reported .

Notably, Ukraine conducted the coordinated strike with primarily Ukrainian developed or adapted technologies. The Financial Times reported that “Ukrainian units involved in the operation deliberately avoided using Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink satellite network,” because of recent US restrictions that prevent Ukraine from using Starshield on drones or anything else traveling more than 100 miles per hour (161 kilometers per hour).

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the latest US-imposed restrictions on Starshield have not yet been lifted , although SpaceX denied that the restrictions had returned. Zelenskyy described the speed limit as interfering with some Ukrainian drone interceptor technologies that were designed to defend against Russian drones attacking Ukrainian cities and infrastructure .

However, the Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Strait Bridge provide yet another example of how the Ukrainian military and defense technology companies have been learning to fight without relying on Starlink . This is also not the first time that Ukraine, arguably the leading country in developing new battlefield uses of drones , has adopted a Russian battlefield innovation for its own uses.

From Russia’s view, the only glimmer of good news may be that the bridge’s railway section was only moderately damaged. The Ukrainian newspaper Kyiv Independent pointed to Russian news and video sources indicating that trains appeared to be running again on the bridge after the strikes.

But the severe damage to the bridge’s arch and roadway section cuts off a crucial transportation and supply link between Russia and the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula of Ukraine. The Institute for the Study of War assesses that the “destruction of the bridge” will complicate Russia’s ability to maintain its occupation and military basing within the peninsula.

The other overland supply route between Russia and Crimea involves highways running through Russian-occupied southern Ukraine. But Ukrainian forces have already been striking such highway infrastructure and the Russian supply trucks running along the exposed route.

Fallen debris from the bridge’s collapsed arch may also prevent any large ship traffic from passing through the Kerch Strait that connects the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea, according to a Telegram channel owner based in Crimea. That makes it even more difficult for Russia to resupply the Crimean peninsula by sea—and Ukrainian drones have previously struck dozens of Russian ships in the Sea of Azov .

Beyond the physical damage to the bridge, such attacks represent a symbolic blow to Putin’s ambition of holding onto the Crimean peninsula. After Russian forces seized Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, Russia based much of its Black Sea Fleet at the naval base in Sevastopol and later used the peninsula as a logistics hub for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The $3.5 billion Kerch Strait Bridge was built as a physical link to cement Russia’s claim over Crimea. Putin personally drove a construction truck across the bridge to commemorate its opening in 2018. He repeated the bridge-crossing feat in a Mercedes in December 2022, after a Ukrainian truck bomb attack temporarily damaged the bridge in October of that year.
In 2025, the bridge was damaged again after Ukraine’s Security Service used agents to plant mines under the bridge supports. Again, Russia repaired the damage.

The Kerch Strait Bridge’s future prospects look much bleaker now following the latest missile and drone strikes. The bridge was initially constructed in two years, and engineering experts told The New York Times that repairs to the bridge roadway could also take two years under normal circumstances. But they also agreed that any damage to the bridge’s piers could extend that repair time—and Russian repair efforts would likely be at risk from future Ukrainian missile and drone attacks.

items.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
paras: Rough day Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick “This time requires leadership and fortitude,” Senator Bill Cassidy said.

26 ... ... ... Heidi Overton, nominee for commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, arrives for a Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee confirmation hearing in Washington, DC, on Sept. 24, 2026. Credit: Getty | Daniel Heuer Heidi Overton, nominee for commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, arrives for a Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee confirmation hearing in Washington, DC, on Sept. 24, 2026. Credit: Getty | Daniel Heuer Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.

Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy’s decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats.

In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA’s current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn’t say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is “quite lethal” or that children are given vaccine doses the “size of a soda bottle.” Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong.
Axios quoted a senior Trump administration official as saying that Overton’s nomination was dropped because she “lacks the support on the Hill to move forward with her confirmation.”

The Senate’s Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, chaired by Bill Cassidy (R-La.), was scheduled to vote on Overton’s nomination Wednesday. In a social media post Tuesday night, after her nomination was withdrawn, Cassidy said he believed she had a “viable confirmation path.” But he said the nomination was “abandoned” after some anti-abortion senators sought commitments from her that they couldn’t get. “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments,” Cassidy said.
“Unfortunately, with the limited time left, confirming a permanent FDA Commissioner will fall to Senate Democrats,” Cassidy noted.
After Overton’s last-minute withdrawal, the HELP committee’s agenda for Wednesday was updated again this morning to scrap a scheduled vote on Jim O’Neill, who was Trump’s nominee to run the NSF.

O’Neill has been criticized for lacking the science experience needed to run the foundation. In the past, O’Neill worked as a Silicon Valley investor and entrepreneur and became a close ally of Peter Thiel. But under Trump, O’Neill has been the deputy secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services and served as acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. O’Neill took over the latter role after the former director, Susan Monarez, was ousted from it less than a month after her Senate confirmation. She later told Senators Kennedy fired her for refusing to blindly approve vaccine recommendations from his anti-vaccine advisors.

In remarks this morning , Cassidy said that O’Neill “did not do enough to stand up for science and against irresponsible decisions and statements from [Health] Secretary [Robert F.] Kennedy [Jr.].” As an example, Cassidy specifically referenced O’Neill’s role in the firing of Monarez. “Several members of the [HELP] committee had concerns regarding this,” Cassidy said.
“This time requires leadership and fortitude and standing up for what is right,” Cassidy added.

The NSF has been hard hit by the Trump administration and actions by Elon Musk’s DOGE. The NSF has been forced to cancel hundreds of research grants and taken brutal cuts to its budget and staff in the past two years. In April, the Trump administration also terminated all members of the board that steers the NSF, called the National Science Board. Former members feared that it would make way for O’Neill to stack the board with political allies, pointing to how Trump filled the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology with tech billionaires —including leaders of Meta, Google, Oracle, and Nvidia—instead of top scientists and researchers.

items.title: Rennae Stubbs responds when asked if Serena Williams will return to tennis in 2027
paras: After months of speculation, the 23-time major singles champion returned to the court at the Queen’s Club Championships, playing alongside Victoria Mboko in the doubles event. It was a successful return to competitive play for the American – she and Mboko defeated third seeds Erin Routliffe and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 7-6, 6-2.

The duo were forced to withdraw from their next match following Mboko’s season-ending injury. Serena made her return to singles play a short while later, losing to Australian youngster Maya Joint in the Wimbledon first round.

The 45-year-old has not played a singles match since making an appearance at the All England Club. I have no idea,” Stubbs, Serena’s coach, said on the Rennae Stubbs Tennis Podcast. “I saw Serena in New York at an event recently other than that I have no idea.

items.title: The five active players who have won the most matches at the ATP Finals in their careers
paras: Alexander Zverev secured his place in the ATP Finals semi-finals after defeating Ben Shelton on Tuesday evening. It was a superb performance by the German, who triumphed 6-2, 7-6 inside the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy.

Zverev clearly has Shelton’s number on the ATP circuit, as evidenced by his 7-0 head-to-head record against the 23-year-old American. Zverev has been one of the most successful players at the ATP Finals over the last decade, winning two titles – in 2018 and 2021 – and reaching the semi-finals at multiple editions of the event.

With Zverev’s excellent record in mind, let us take a look at how other active players have performed at the event during their respective careers. According to statisticians OptaAce , Novak Djokovic leads all other players in this particular statistical area.

items.title: “The saddest match of my career”: Cobolli fights back tears after his Turin exit
paras: Anyone who has spent time around Flavio Cobolli knows the Italian is all in: generous, wholehearted, fully committed to his tennis dream. By far the defining image of these ATP Finals so far, his fight to hold back the tears in his press conference after losing to Frances Tiafoe , 7-6(6), 6-0 on Wednesday night, felt like the logical consequence of the evening.

“This is definitely the match that makes me the saddest of my career,” the Italian said quietly. The world No 6, a Roland-Garros finalist this year, is out of the ATP Finals in Turin on his debut, at home, without winning a set.
The question that brought him close to tears was not about the match but about his season. He asked for it to be repeated, seemingly to buy time.

items.title: Lindsay Davenport reacts as Team USA player tears ACL before Billie Jean King Cup tie, ‘that’s a loss for us’
paras: Team USA will play Hungary in a Billie Jean King Cup play-off tie from November 21 to November 22 in Delray Beach, Florida. The Americans will be without one of their top doubles players, though, after Nicole Melichar-Martinez tore her ACL at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

Another doubles specialist, Desirae Krawczyk, has replaced her. Team USA Billie Jean King Cup captain, Lindsay Davenport , has delivered her verdict on Melichar-Martinez’s injury and commented on home favourite Coco Gauff, issuing a fitness update on the two-time Grand Slam champion.

Which of these four WTA players do you think is most likely to win a Grand Slam in 2027? Des Krawczyk agreed at the last minute, when Nicole got hurt, to come, so we’re sending all of our best wishes to Nicole.”

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
